text:
maya: Heads up, console shows a cluster of rejects for tool="event_router" on route="exp-routing-v3". Reject reasons: "parse_error" and "unexpected_type". Anyone touching event_router recently?

diego: Can you paste a minimal example from logs?

maya: Sample (from compressed logs):
```
{
  "req": "r-9f3",
  "tool": "event_router",
  "error": "unexpected_type",
  "expected": "object(fields: [type,payload])",
  "actual": "{\"type\":\"click\",\"payload\":\"id=123\"}"
}
```
Note: actual looks like a JSON-encoded string instead of a nested object.

sam: That usually happens when the model variant returns a text blob (string) with escape sequences rather than structured JSON. Did we deploy a faster tokenizer variant?

jo: I rolled a model tag last night that added a compacting pass. Could be serializing the object into a string to save tokens. Shouldn't have hit exp-routing-v3 though.

maya: Query I ran: `select * from invokes where tool='event_router' and ts > now() - interval '6 hours' and reject=true order by ts desc limit 100;` shows about ~120 rejects, mostly from exp-routing-v3.

diego: Immediate options: 1) adapter can attempt to detect JSON-in-string and parse once (coerce=true) and mark as soft-reject; 2) route fallback to stable-variant; 3) revert model tag.

sam: Also: do these rejects impact billing or SLA alerts? Support got pages.f

billing-bot: Alert: derived 502 pages for acct=cli-start due to invokes.rejects spike

jo: We treat validation rejects as non-billable, but some alerting pipelines use invoke.rejects as a hard signal. We need clearer telemetry to avoid false pages.

diego: Telemetry plan: add `validation_reason` (string), `validation_action` (blocked|coerced|ignored), `coercion` boolean flag, and `payload_sample_redacted` for sampled full payloads (1%). Also a histogram `rejects_by_route`.

maya: UX: console needs a quick filter for `validation_action=coerced` and show both raw and coerced payloads inline with a small note: "coercion applied - parsed JSON string to object" with a link to the raw log S3.

sam: Short-term mitigation: I propose adapter parse-once for JSON-like strings and set coercion=true. This reduces pages and gives time to revert tag. But we must log both original_raw and parsed_payload so we can audit.

jo: Agreed, but add a TTL: 4 hours max for this shim so we don't mask regressions too long. Also add an automated job to run sample canonical prompts against the new model tag in CI; fail the rollout if any output is string-encoded JSON for tools that expect structured object.

diego: I'll push a telemetry PR and a small metric to alert if coercion rate > 0.2% for 15m.

maya: I'll open adapter PR to attempt parse-coercion and include trace flag `coercion=parse_json_string`. Will deploy to exp-routing-v3 only.

deploy-bot: deploy started: adapter-parsecoerce-v1 -> exp-routing-v3 (initiated by maya) :truck:

billing-bot: Billing alerts muted for validation rejects for 30 minutes (muted by sam)

jo: Also making a console enhancement ticket: show a diff between expected schema and example (render both pretty). One-click rollback to previous model tag is on the wishlist.

diego: Action items: 1) maya deploy shim to route, 2) diego add telemetry + alert, 3) jo add preflight schema check in model push CI, 4) sam mute billing/alerts and watch, 5) maya add raw/parsed payload logging for audit.

maya: PR is up: github.com/redwood/adapter/pull/821 - tests green, deploying now.

diego: Telemetry PR merged. Sampling set to 1% for full payloads, redact PII.

maya: Shim live on exp-routing-v3. Seeing immediate reduction in pages. Will monitor for 2 hours and then either revert model tag or proceed with rollback if coercion rate stays high.

jo: Thanks. We'll follow up with a short RCA if rollback occurs; otherwise a blameless note and a preflight check added to model pipeline.
